reviews.title: LEBARA - Poor service & appalling customer care - Avoid LEBARA!
reviews.body:
LEBARA Customer Service is 'NOT FIT FOR PURPOSE'!
On 28-10-2026 I requested a replacement for my lost SIM through my on-line account. LEBARA stated that the replacement SIM will be despatched by 1st Class Post. 
On 30-10-2026, LEBARA Customer Service was informed that the SIM has not yet been received. They said it was despatched by 1st Class Post on the day it was requested but failed to provide any assuarance of delivery. 
On 31-10-2026 when LEBARA Customer Service was contacted again, they said that delivery can take up to 5-working-days! 
On 02-11-2026 LEBARA Customer Service was contacted again. They failed to say when the SIM will be delivered.
On 03-11-2026 LEBARA Customer Service was contacted again. As they failed again to say when the SIM will be delivered, a formal complaint was made.
On 04-11-2026 LEBARA Customer Service phoned. After going through the customer authentication process, instead of dealing with the matter, he said that he needs to put the call on hold to establish details regarding the issue! He failed to justify why it was not done beforehand instead of inconveniencing and wasting customer's time! When he eventually came back, he failed to answer simple questions. He kept repeating what has already been established. He failed to provide any action towards a resolution. When mentioned that he was acting in a totally  incompetent and unprofessional manner he just said that the issue will be escalated and hung-up!
This is totally unacceptable and shoddy Customer Care. Absolutely SHAMEFUL! Avoid LEBARA!

reviews.title: Appalling
reviews.body:
Appalling, unreliable service and virtually impossible to get help

I have experienced repeated problems with Lebara over the years, particularly when travelling in Europe. On several occasions, mobile data simply stopped working abroad. When I previously contacted customer service by phone for assistance, I received no meaningful help and was instead treated rudely.

Now things have reached an entirely unacceptable level.

Since 20 October 2026, I have been completely unable to make OR receive telephone calls while in Hungary, despite having an active, paid mobile plan. For over two weeks, nobody has been able to reach me by phone, and I have been unable to call anyone.

I reported the problem by email and received no response. Lebara’s online complaint form repeatedly fails with CAPTCHA errors, and its live chat is inaccessible. Even trying to submit a formal complaint has become an ordeal.

To make matters worse, I received an unexpected email containing a verification code for transferring my number to a new SIM — something I NEVER requested or authorised.

I am now demanding a refund, compensation and an urgent investigation.

I previously posted a negative Trustpilot review about Lebara’s service, but it was removed after I declined to provide additional identifying information for verification.

A mobile provider that leaves paying customers unreachable abroad for weeks, fails to respond to complaints and makes customer support practically inaccessible is unworthy of its customers’ trust or loyalty.

I would strongly advise anyone who relies on their phone while travelling to think very carefully before choosing Lebara.

Update — 4 November 2026: Appalling complaint handling

On 3 November, I spent nearly an hour in live chat with Lebara customer service, repeatedly explaining that I had been unable to make or receive telephone calls since 20 October, despite paying for an active plan.

I also raised a serious security concern about an unexpected SIM-transfer verification notification that I had never requested, and asked for an investigation, a refund and compensation.

Despite repeatedly asking the adviser to confirm that all these issues had been recorded and escalated, I never received a clear answer. I was given reference CAS-2980314-F6K4M9 and promised contact within 24 hours. I also tried to download the chat transcript, but the download never completed.

The following morning, Lebara emailed me claiming they had tried to telephone me but my phone was switched off, and asked me to provide another number so they could call me.

My phone was NOT switched off. The entire reason for my complaint is that my Lebara SIM cannot receive calls!

After nearly an hour explaining this to customer service the previous evening, receiving such a response was astonishing.

This has left me unreachable for more than two weeks while expecting important medical, housing-related and official calls. The uncertainty about what I may have missed has caused considerable anxiety, distress and disruption.

I have now submitted a formal written complaint. I still have no explanation for the service failure, no meaningful response to the SIM-security concern, and no resolution.

I expect Lebara to investigate properly, restore the service, address the security issue and provide an appropriate refund and compensation.

Customers should not have to spend hours explaining a basic service failure only to receive a response that demonstrates their complaint has not been understood.

UPDATE — 5 November 2026

Following Lebara’s public response, I contacted the escalation address provided by John-Paul Patten, Business Operations Director.

I STILL CANNOT MAKE OR RECEIVE CALLS, a problem ongoing since 20 October despite my paid plan remaining active.

I have sent numerous emails, spent nearly an hour in live chat, submitted a formal complaint and reported the matter to Ofcom. My concerns about an unsolicited SIM-transfer verification notification also remain unanswered.

Despite all these efforts, I have received no meaningful technical assistance, no resolution, no explanation, no refund and no compensation.

I have exhausted considerable time and energy trying to obtain a service I have already paid for. I should not have to continue chasing a telecommunications provider simply to make it fulfil its basic obligations.

I am leaving this matter to the appropriate independent authorities and dispute-resolution bodies.
